newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Paragon Union trading limits lifted.
newsitem.headline: Paragon Union trading limits lifted.

text.p: Trading limits in the stock of Paragon Union Bhd will be lifted starting from Monday, the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) said on Friday.

The stock had been declared a "designated" security by the KLSE with effect from November 12, which meant, among other things, that sellers had to first deliver shares of the company to their stockbroker before any sales were allowed.
Included in the restriction is that buyers of the stock must pay the full amount up front to the stockbroking firm for the purchase.
In essence, the designation makes it more difficult to trade in the stock. The KLSE did not give a reason for the lifting of the restriction in its statement on Friday.
In the past, the exchange has designated stocks in order to cool speculative trading excesses.
Paragon Union's businesses include making car carpets and automotive components, precision machining and metal stamping.
Its stock closed at 16.20 ringgit on Friday, up 10 cents. Its year high is 24.00 ringgit.
